title: write through a stale pointer, with no allocation between the free and the use
object: a, 24 bytes, freed and then written
control: the same single alloc and single free, with the write before the free instead of after it

asan.why: THE ANNOTATION-FEASIBILITY ROW. ASan's quarantine and shadow catch it on malloc. A bump-pointer arena cannot poison on free because st_free does not know the object's size (allocators/arena/arena.c TODO), so even the annotated arena stays blind -- an annotation arm can fail for reasons of allocator DESIGN, not of tool support. A free list knows the size class, so its annotated arm works.

valgrind.why: Same split, via VALGRIND_MEMPOOL_FREE, which the arena never calls.

hwasan.why: malloc retags on free, so the stale pointer's tag no longer matches. HWASan has no public custom-allocator interface, so the annotated columns are UNSUPPORTED, not MISSED (C3.4).

ubsan.why: -fsanitize=bounds needs a statically known array bound; a pointer out of an allocator has none. The row is kept so the report can say UBSan is not a heap tool rather than leaving it out.

lowfat.why: LowFat checks bounds only; it has no notion of a lifetime.

status: written, smoke-run on malloc and arena; server run pending (A5)
